result:
No actions this turn. Writing the design is next, but one choice still belongs to you first: how it gets built. Every question so far was about what you want.

---

Understood, I'll write it up. One decision first, because the design depends on it. Your time on the floor is the expensive part, so this is the only question before I write.

There are two sensible ways to build this on what you already run:

1. **Add it to the existing taproom app** (my recommendation). New pages and tables in the same Flask app and SQLite database on the office Pi. A cheap USB barcode scanner works like a keyboard, so scanning a sack's lot number needs no special software. The label printer hangs off the same machine. This keeps one thing to run, back up, and fix. The downside is that a bug in batch tracking could take the tabs down with it, so the two parts would be kept clearly separate inside the app.

2. **A separate small app on the same Pi**, with its own database. Tabs and traceability can't affect each other. The cost is a second thing to keep running and back up, and a second set of pages to log into.

I ruled out off-the-shelf brewery software. You'd be adapting your process to someone else's model of a batch, and you've told me exactly what yours is.

This is project-sized, so the design will be a full written document. A reviewer will read it before you see it and may come back once with a few questions. After you approve it, the build gets planned in a fresh session.

Which way do you want to go, with the existing app or a separate one?
